items.title: Section: Skilful Mastery of the Five Fields and Three Categories of Teaching, and Wisdom Working for Every Being — Comprehensive Wisdom Closes

items.zh: 若諸菩薩，於五明處決定善巧，廣說如前力種性品，應知其相。及於三聚中決定善巧，謂於能引義利法聚、能引非義利法聚、能引非義利非非義利法聚，皆如實知。於是八處所有妙慧善巧攝受，能速圓滿廣大無上妙智資糧，速證無上正等菩提。能作一切有情義利慧有十一種，如前應知。即於彼位所有妙慧，當知是名饒益有情慧。
items.en: Bodhisattvas possess decisive skill in the five classical fields of knowledge, as described more fully in an earlier chapter, and one should understand their character accordingly. They likewise possess decisive skill regarding three categories of teaching: teachings that genuinely lead towards liberation and benefit, teachings that lead only towards harm, and teachings that lead towards neither benefit nor harm — all genuinely and correctly understood as such. Genuinely skilful, well-gathered wisdom across these eight areas swiftly perfects the vast, unsurpassed accumulation of wisdom needed for supreme awakening, and swiftly brings that awakening about. Wisdom actively working for the benefit of every being is of eleven kinds, as should be understood from what was already described earlier; the genuinely excellent wisdom present in each of those eleven activities should be understood as wisdom benefiting sentient beings.

items.title: Section: The Wisdom of Difficult Practice — Knowing Emptiness Itself, Skilfully Taming Any Being, and Freedom From Every Obstruction to Complete Knowledge

items.zh: 云何菩薩難行慧？當知此慧略有三種。若諸菩薩能知甚深法無我智，是名第一難行慧。若諸菩薩能了有情調伏方便智，是名第二難行慧。若諸菩薩了知一切所知境界無障礙智，是名第三最難行慧。
items.en: What is a bodhisattva's wisdom of difficult practice? One should know this wisdom is, in brief, of three kinds. Bodhisattvas who genuinely know the profound wisdom of the selflessness of phenomena — this is called the first wisdom of difficult practice. Bodhisattvas who thoroughly understand the skilful means of taming beings — this is called the second wisdom of difficult practice. Bodhisattvas who know, entirely without obstruction, every possible object of knowledge — this is called the third and most difficult wisdom of difficult practice.

items.title: Section: Comprehensive-Gateway Wisdom — Fluent in Both Canons, and the Three Non-Conceptual Wisdoms United

items.zh: 云何菩薩一切門慧？當知此慧略有四種。謂於聲聞藏及菩薩藏，所有勝妙聞所成慧、思所成慧，於能思擇菩薩所應作應隨轉中，及菩薩所不應作應止息中，思擇力所攝慧，及修習力所攝三摩呬多地無量慧。
items.en: What is a bodhisattva's comprehensive-gateway wisdom? One should know this wisdom is, in brief, of four kinds: genuinely excellent wisdom born of hearing, spanning both the śrāvaka canon and the bodhisattva canon; genuinely excellent wisdom born of reflection, likewise spanning both; wisdom belonging to the power of deliberate reflection, correctly discerning what a bodhisattva should actively pursue and what should instead be set aside; and immeasurable wisdom belonging to the power of genuine meditative cultivation within absorption itself.

items.title: Section: Virtuous-Person Wisdom — Ten Marks Told Two Different Ways

items.zh: 云何菩薩善士慧？當知此慧略有五種。一、聽聞正法所集成慧，二、內正作意俱行慧，三、自他利行方便俱行慧，四、於諸法法住、法安立無顛倒中善決定慧，五、捨煩惱慧。復有異門。一、微細慧，悟入所知如所有性故。二、周備慧，悟入所知盡所有性故。三、俱生慧，宿智資糧所集成故。四、具教慧，能於諸佛、已入大地諸菩薩眾所聞法義具受持故。五、具證慧，從淨意樂地乃至到究竟地所攝受故。
items.en: What is a bodhisattva's virtuous-person wisdom? One should know this wisdom is, in brief, of five kinds. First, wisdom gathered through hearing the true teaching. Second, wisdom accompanying genuinely correct reflection. Third, wisdom skilled in the actual means of benefiting both self and others. Fourth, decisive wisdom that correctly and without distortion grasps how phenomena abide and are constituted. Fifth, wisdom that releases affliction. There is, further, another way of categorising this same wisdom: first, subtle wisdom, penetrating the true nature of what can be known; second, comprehensive wisdom, grasping the full extent of what can be known; third, wisdom carried forward from past cultivation, gathered from prior lifetimes' own store of wisdom; fourth, wisdom thoroughly grounded in received teaching, fully retaining what has been heard directly from buddhas and from bodhisattvas already established on the grounds; fifth, wisdom matured through actual attainment, gathered continuously from the ground of genuinely pure aspiration all the way to the very final ground.

items.title: Section: Comprehensive-Kind Wisdom — the Classical Path-Knowledges, From the Four Truths to a Buddha's Own Ten Powers

items.zh: 云何菩薩一切種慧？當知此慧，六種、七種，總十三種。六種慧者，謂於諸諦苦智、集智、滅智、道智，於究竟位盡智、無生智，是名六慧。七種慧者，謂法智、類智、世俗智、神通智、相智、十力前行智、四道理中正道理智。
items.en: What is a bodhisattva's comprehensive-kind wisdom? One should know this wisdom is, in brief, of thirteen kinds altogether — six of one sort and seven of another. The six are: with respect to the truths, the knowledge of suffering, the knowledge of its origin, the knowledge of its cessation, and the knowledge of the path, together with, at the very culmination, the knowledge that affliction is exhausted and the knowledge that no further rebirth in bondage will occur — these are the six wisdoms. The seven are: dharma-knowledge, subsequent knowledge, conventional knowledge, the knowledge of supernormal powers, the knowledge of characteristics, the knowledge preceding a buddha's ten powers, and the knowledge of correct reasoning among the four kinds of reasoning.

items.title: Section: Fulfilling-Requests Wisdom — the Four Unimpeded Understandings, and "Neither Suchness Nor Coming" Applied to Buddha, Arhat, Bodhisattva, and Ordinary Being

items.zh: 云何菩薩遂求慧？當知此慧略有八種。一、依法異門智，所謂菩薩法無礙慧。二、依法相智，所謂菩薩義無礙慧。三、依法釋詞智，所謂菩薩釋詞無礙慧。四、依法品類句差別智，所謂菩薩辯才無礙慧。五、菩薩一切摧伏他論慧。六、菩薩一切成立自論慧。七、菩薩一切正訓營為家屬家產慧。八、菩薩一切善解種種王正世務慧。
items.en: What is a bodhisattva's fulfilling-requests wisdom? One should know this wisdom is, in brief, of eight kinds. First, wisdom grounded in the varied synonyms of the teaching — a bodhisattva's unimpeded wisdom regarding the teaching itself. Second, wisdom grounded in the actual characteristics phenomena bear — a bodhisattva's unimpeded wisdom regarding their genuine meaning. Third, wisdom grounded in explaining the teaching in any language — a bodhisattva's unimpeded wisdom in linguistic explanation. Fourth, wisdom grounded in every distinct category and classification a teaching might use — a bodhisattva's unimpeded eloquence. Fifth, a bodhisattva's wisdom capable of refuting every rival argument. Sixth, a bodhisattva's wisdom capable of establishing every genuine argument of their own. Seventh, a bodhisattva's wisdom in correctly instructing family members and correctly managing household property. Eighth, a bodhisattva's wisdom skilfully understanding every kind of governmental and worldly affair.

items.title: Section: Both-Worlds-Happiness Wisdom — the Five Fields Mastered Without Attachment, Matched to Four Kinds of Being

items.zh: 云何菩薩此世他世樂慧？當知此慧略有九種。謂諸菩薩，於內明處，能善明淨、善安住慧；於醫方明處、因明處、聲明處、世工業明處，能善明淨、非安住慧。一切菩薩，即用如是於五明處善明淨慧以為依止，於他愚癡、放逸、怯弱、勤修正行所化有情，如其次第，示現、教導、讚勵、慶慰慧。
items.en: What is a bodhisattva's wisdom of happiness in this world and the next? One should know this wisdom is, in brief, of nine kinds. Bodhisattvas possess genuine, luminous, settled and confidently grounded wisdom regarding inner wisdom; and genuine, luminous wisdom, though without any settled attachment, regarding medicine, logic, linguistics, and the practical arts. Relying on this genuine, luminous wisdom across the five classical fields, bodhisattvas apply, in turn, wisdom that reveals genuine understanding to confused beings, wisdom that corrects careless beings, wisdom that encourages faint-hearted beings, and wisdom that warmly congratulates beings already diligently engaged in genuine practice.

items.title: Section: Ten Purity Wisdoms, Five Pairs — Closing the Wisdom Chapter and All Six Perfections as One Complete Whole

items.zh: 云何菩薩清淨慧？當知此慧略有十種。於真實義有二種慧。謂由盡所有性及如所有性取真實義故。於流轉義有二種慧。謂取正因果故。於執受義有二種慧。謂顛倒、不顛倒，如實了知故。於方便義有二種慧。謂一切所應作、所不應作，如實了知故。於究竟義有二種慧。謂雜染，如實了知雜染故；清淨，如實了知清淨故。如是菩薩五義十種差別淨慧，當知是名最勝淨慧。如是菩薩極善決定無量妙慧，能證菩薩大菩提果。菩薩依此，能圓滿慧波羅蜜多，速證無上正等菩提。
items.en: What is a bodhisattva's purity wisdom? One should know this wisdom is, in brief, of ten kinds. Regarding genuine reality, there are two kinds of wisdom: grasping genuine reality both through its full extent and through its true nature. Regarding the process of conditioned arising, there are two kinds of wisdom: correctly grasping genuine cause and effect. Regarding what is genuinely received as teaching, there are two kinds of wisdom: correctly discerning what is distorted and what is not. Regarding the actual means of the path, there are two kinds of wisdom: correctly discerning what should and should not be done. Regarding the final goal, there are two kinds of wisdom: correctly understanding affliction as affliction, and correctly understanding genuine purity as purity. These ten distinct kinds of pure wisdom, spanning these five dimensions of meaning, should be understood as a bodhisattva's own most excellent, pure wisdom. Wisdom of this kind, genuinely excellent and decisively settled, immeasurable and wondrous, brings about a bodhisattva's great fruit of awakening. Relying on this, bodhisattvas fulfil the perfection of wisdom, and swiftly realise supreme, complete awakening.

blocks.text: The remaining aspects of wisdom, closing the perfections.
Wisdom skilled in the five fields and in the three categories of teaching: "eight bases" in all (Venerable Miào Jìng).

"Knowing the profound selflessness of phenomena; understanding the skilful means of taming beings; unobstructed knowledge of all knowables." Venerable Miào Jìng: three barriers crossed: between ordinary and noble, lesser and great, cause and fruit.
Wisdom from hearing and reflection across both canons; contaminated and uncontaminated wisdom from cultivation.
Knowledge of the four truths; at the culmination, knowledge of exhaustion and non-arising; up to a Buddha's ten powers. Master Cháng Bǎi explains Dharma-knowledge.

Of the teaching's terms, its meanings, its languages, and eloquence. And a riddle: "beings come but are not thus; arhats are thus but do not come; bodhisattvas are both thus and coming; the Buddha is neither". Master Cháng Bǎi explains it.

Wisdom "clear and well settled" in inner science; clear in medicine, logic, linguistics, and crafts. Towards the deluded, careless, faint-hearted, and diligent: revealing, teaching, encouraging, congratulating.
Ten kinds, in five pairs, regarding reality, conditioned arising, appropriation, means, and culmination. Venerable Miào Jìng: "reality" is purified suchness.

quiz.q: What are the three kinds of difficult wisdom?
options: knowing the profound selflessness of phenomena, understanding the means to tame beings, unobstructed knowledge of all knowables
quiz.why: Knowing the profound selflessness of phenomena; understanding the skilful means of taming beings; unobstructed knowledge of all knowable objects. Master Cháng Bǎi: those who haven't realised the emptiness of phenomena still have many inversions.

quiz.q: Why is knowing the profound selflessness of phenomena difficult, according to the two lectures?
options: Cháng Bǎi: it is the barrier between ordinary and noble — citing "why not eat meat porridge?" for the inversions of the unrealized; Miào Jìng: ordinary beings' grasping is too strong to break easily
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: this is the barrier between ordinary and noble — like the emperor who asked, "Why not eat meat porridge?" Venerable Miào Jìng: ordinary beings' grasping at something to be gained is too strong; breaking it is very hard.

quiz.q: How do the two lectures explain the third (reflection-power) and fourth (cultivation-power) wisdoms?
options: Cháng Bǎi citing Ce: contaminated vs. uncontaminated cultivation-wisdom; Miào Jìng: insight practised within calm vs. the wisdom of acceptance of non-arising
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi, citing Ce in the 《瑜伽論記》: the third is contaminated cultivation-wisdom, the fourth uncontaminated. Venerable Miào Jìng: the third is the reflective power of insight practised within calm — cultivation-wisdom; the fourth is the wisdom of acceptance of non-arising after cultivation succeeds.

quiz.q: What are the six wisdoms of comprehensive-kind wisdom?
options: knowledge of suffering, origin, cessation, path, and at the culmination, knowledge of exhaustion and non-arising
quiz.why: "With respect to the truths, knowledge of suffering, origin, cessation, and path; and at the culmination, knowledge of exhaustion and non-arising." Master Cháng Bǎi: the knowledge of exhaustion and non-arising attained at the arhat's stage beyond training.

quiz.q: On unobstructed eloquence, the lectures use a four-line "suchness/coming" formula. What is it?
options: beings come but are not thus; arhats are thus but don't come; bodhisattvas are both; the Buddha neither
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: beings come but are not thus; arhats are thus but do not come; bodhisattvas are both thus and coming; the Buddha is neither. Venerable Miào Jìng: the Buddha is inconceivable — "neither thus nor coming, hence Tathāgata."

quiz.q: Relying on clear wisdom in the five fields, how does the bodhisattva treat the deluded, the careless, the faint-hearted, and the diligent, respectively?
quiz.why: Towards the deluded, careless, faint-hearted, and diligent, "in that order, revealing, teaching, encouraging, and congratulating." Master Cháng Bǎi: a disciple accomplished in virtue and learning should be congratulated and encouraged.

quiz.q: Purity wisdom has "ten kinds under five meanings." What are the five?
options: reality, conditioned arising, appropriation, means, culmination
quiz.why: Two wisdoms each regarding reality, conditioned arising, appropriation, means, and culmination. Venerable Miào Jìng: "reality" refers to pure dependent origination; "conditioned arising" to the dependent origination of saṃsāra.
